subject: Urgent: production regressions impacting Finova — SLA remedies & next steps
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@finova.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@finova.com>
Cc: Danielle Price <dani.price@finova.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent 503s and slow responses since Thursday night

Hi Aisha,

We're seeing intermittent 5xx responses and elevated tail latency in production starting Thursday ~22:30 PST. A few quick datapoints:
- Error rate (5xx) spiked to 3.8% for a 45-min window (normally <0.1%).
- p50 ~ 90ms, p95 increased from ~250ms to ~2.1s during the spike.
- End-to-end throughput dropped ~25% for the same window; some requests timed out on our side.

We attached a sample of request traces and the gateway logs that show 503 errors. This is customer-facing and causing failed payment flows for a subset of users. Can you confirm cause and an ETA for a fix? Also want to understand expected SLA remedy — last month we hit committed throughput and this outage materially impacted volumes.

Attachments: error_snapshot.png, p50_latency_logs_20260220.zip

Regards,
Sophie Lang
VP Engineering, Finova

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@finova.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@finova.com>

Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s and slow responses since Thursday night

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm escalating this to our incident team now. Quick plan:

1) Triage call in 30 minutes (I've invited our on-call SE).
2) We'll pull job-level telemetry and look for scheduling/queueing anomalies.
3) I'll follow up with an initial impact summary and proposed immediate mitigations within 2 hours.

Can you confirm whether the failing requests are pinned to a specific region/route or random across sessions? That will help narrow the surface.

Cc'ing Sergio (SE) to join triage. We will also collect the billing window and impacted traffic for SLA calculations.

Short call now? 09:45?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman

Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent 503s and slow responses since Thursday night — Finova impact and next steps

Team — forwarding Finova's note and the logs we collected during triage. Summary of what happened and customer asks:

- Incident window: 2026-02-19 22:30 PST — 2026-02-20 00:00 PST (roughly 90 minutes).
- Customer impact: failed payment flows for a small % of users; they want remediation, a clear root cause, and an SLA credit calculation.
- External asks: immediate mitigation timeline + formal credit proposal and contract amendment if applicable.

What I need from you:
- Rishi: preliminary root cause and candidate remediation steps; build a credit calc using our SLA formula (attach spreadsheet).
- Sergio: tally whether any infra/serving config changes were deployed around the window.
- Evelyn: recommend whether we escalate to Executive cover (Finova wants legal/contract-level certainty).
- Markus: want to flag this in case we need exec outreach; customer is on a strategic path to expand.

Please reply with your inputs by EOD tomorrow. Attaching the incident artifacts we pulled.

Forwarded attachments: p50_latency_logs_20260220.zip

Thanks,
Aisha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 08:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 503s and slow responses since Thursday night — RCA and credit calc

Team — preliminary RCA and credit math below. Attaching SLA worksheet (sla_credit_calc.xlsx) and a short remediation runbook (remediation_runbook.md).

Preliminary RCA:
- Root cause: cache invalidation cascade + scheduler race. On heavy concurrent prefix invalidations we observed KV cache thrashing which caused backpressure in the serving scheduler. That, combined with an unlucky scheduling decision, led to increased queuing and some requests hitting our global timeout path (503).
- Contributing factors: a recent change to the cache eviction heuristic (deployed 2026-02-18) increased eviction aggressiveness under bursty writes.

Immediate mitigation (performed):
- Rolled back the heuristic change at 00:20 PST; rehydrated hot prefixes from backup cache.
- Increased short-term concurrency headroom for the affected pool.

Proposed remediation (next 7 business days):
1) Permanent revert and QA for the eviction heuristic.
2) Add guardrails in scheduler to prevent global timeout paths on backpressure spikes.
3) Improve monitoring and automated throttles for prefix invalidations.

SLA credit calculation (worksheet attached):
- Using Finova's committed monthly spend and our SLA schedule, preliminary credit = 6% of monthly invoice for the impacted billing period. See sla_credit_calc.xlsx for line-by-line math.

I recommend proposing the 6% credit plus a commitment timeline and a contract addendum that documents the remediation milestones and a mediated review in 30 days.

Attachments: sla_credit_calc.xlsx, remediation_runbook.md

- Rishi
Sr. Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@finova.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@finova.com>, Danielle Price <dani.price@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production regressions impacting Finova — SLA remedies & next steps

Aisha — thanks for the RCA and the quick rollback. I reviewed Rishi's credit worksheet. Our view: the customer impact here is larger than a short window suggests because we measured downstream payment retries and customer support volume tied to the incident. We believe a 6% credit is insufficient.

Our ask: 12% credit for the impacted invoice + a written commitment to a non-escalation playbook (we need higher confidence on throttling and a postmortem with runbook changes). Also want the remediation timeline condensed (3 business days for the critical fixes) and a formal Exec-to-Exec note acknowledging the breach and the proposed remedy. If we can't get terms aligned quickly we will pause planned expansion and escalate to procurement/legal for contract leverage.

On the call this morning we also asked for samples of request IDs and the end-to-end traces — I still need the combined trace bundle (not just p50 logs). Can you provide that?

Thanks,
Sophie

Subject: Re: Urgent: production regressions impacting Finova — SLA remedies & next steps

Sophie — thank you for the clear feedback and for providing downstream impact details. I own this on behalf of Redwood leadership and want to propose a path forward that balances remediation speed with a fair contractual resolution.

What Redwood will provide:
- Credit: we will issue a 9% service credit against Finova's impacted billing period. This is higher than the initial calc and reflects downstream disruption you described.
- Timeline: commit to the critical code fix and scheduler guardrails within 3 business days; full QA and monitoring improvements within 10 business days. Rishi and his team will share daily status updates until completion.
- Postmortem & runbook: a written postmortem and runbook changes delivered within 7 business days, with a joint review session between teams.
- Contract amendment: we'll produce a short amendment documenting the credit and remediation milestones. We'll route this via DocuSign (link below) for signature.

DocuSign link for the amendment: https://docusign.redwood.com/ABC-Remedy-2026
Drive folder with traces and artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/Finova/incident_20260220
HubSpot deal reference: HS:deal:FIN-3241

If this is acceptable we will prepare the amendment and schedule a C-level call to close the loop. If you need a larger credit, please propose a specific number and we will take that back to legal for review; my expectation is 9% is a reasonable middle ground that we can sign today.

Again, I'm sorry for the disruption. We'll prioritize this and I will join the joint review personally.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
